subject: Align on model candidates & perf pack for OrbitAI pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orbitai.com>, Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@orbitai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Align on model candidates & perf pack for OrbitAI pilot

Thanks for a great demo this morning — appreciate the clear context on the search+RAG workload and the 95th%-ile latency constraint you mentioned (target p95 <= 220ms for short queries). Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get a pilot scheduled: 

Summary: 
- Workload: mixed short search queries (~20–80 tokens) plus occasional long-context summarization (up to 6k tokens) in infrequent batches.
- Primary risks: quality regressions on domain-specific medical taxonomy, and tail latency for short queries under burst.

Redwood-verified model candidates (recommended shortlist):
1) rw-open-13b-quant (low-cost, 200 t/s steady-state @8k context cached, p95 ~180ms on g5-2x)
2) rw-llama2-70b-latency (quantized variant for low p95, 35 t/s steady-state, p95 ~160–210ms depending on concurrency)
3) rw-stream-30b (best trade for long-context summarization; p99 spikes with 6k contexts — expect 2–3s p99 in unconstrained runs)

Attachments I’m sharing: orbitai_perf_profiles.pdf (Redwood-verified TPS/latency snapshots per model), orbitai_promptset_v1.jsonl (seed prompts we used for your taxonomy). I’ve also published a live snapshot of the perf runs: https://redwood.app/bench/DASH-9087-orbitai 

Suggested next steps: 
- You: confirm which two models you want in the pilot (suggest rw-open-13b-quant + rw-stream-30b)
- We: run a short targeted bench with your promptset and a simulated burst profile (we can reuse the prompts you shared) and deliver per-model TPS/p95/p99 and cost estimates.
- Legal/Proc: I’ll send a short SOW and pilot statement-of-work link once we lock model slate.

If this looks right I can kick off the bench today and loop Solutions (Monica) to scope the test harness + monitoring. Proposed pilot kickoff window: next Monday (08/16) — does that work for you?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: orbitai_perf_profiles.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
Attachment: orbitai_promptset_v1.jsonl (JSONL, 18KB)

From: Samir Patel <samir@orbitai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@orbitai.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Align on model candidates & perf pack for OrbitAI pilot

Thanks Ben — great recap and thanks for the suggested slate. Two quick clarifying questions before we lock models: 
1) For the rw-open-13b-quant numbers you listed, what was the average request length assumed (prompt + completion)? If you can include a short-run where we bias toward short queries (15–40 tokens) that would be helpful.
2) For the long-context runs, does Redwood’s caching (prefix/KV) materially reduce cost/latency for repeated documents or will those remain expensive for summarization flows?

If those answers look good here we’re happy to proceed with the two-model pilot. Monday 08/16 is fine for a kickoff — we’ll book a recurring 30m sync after the first bench snapshot.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, OrbitAI
Attachment: none

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orbitai.com>, Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@orbitai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Align on model candidates & perf pack for OrbitAI pilot

Samir — quick answers and proposal: 
1) rw-open-13b-quant baseline: the numbers in the perf PDF assume 28 tokens average (prompt+completion). I ran a short variant biased to 25 tokens average for short-query simulation and saw a ~12% improvement in steady TPS and a ~15–25ms improvement on p95. We’ll run the exact 15–40 token distribution you asked for in the targeted bench.
2) Caching: yes — prefix/KV caching gives large wins for repeated document retrievals. For repeated-context summarization (same doc across requests) we see cost reductions of ~30–45% and p95 improvements of ~100–300ms depending on model and cache hit rate (we included a cache vs no-cache snapshot in perf_snapshot_20270809.csv). For the long single-shot summarizations caching doesn’t help (one-off doc).

Action items I’ll kick off today: 
- Run bench with OrbitAI prompt distribution (15–40 tokens short queries + 6k long-context samples) and publish a short CSV snapshot (perf_snapshot_20270809.csv) — ETA EOD today.
- Open HubSpot pilot record: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/DEAL-2027-0345 (I added proposed pilot success criteria).
- Draft SOW/DocuSign link for the pilot (I’ll attach once legal OKs).

Would you prefer the pilot to include auto-fallback to a lower-cost model under heavy concurrency, or do you want to measure without fallbacks first? Fallbacks affect quality consistency (we can gate them behind canary rules).

Thanks — will ping once the CSV + bench dashboard is live.

Ben
Attachment: perf_snapshot_20270809.csv (CSV, 9KB)
Related link: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/DEAL-2027-0345

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitAI pilot — bench ask + regression guardrails (internal)

Internal note — looping you both to scope the bench and get Solutions/CS ready for the pilot kickoff next Monday. External thread above for reference. Key points for our runbook: 
- Bench profile: 70% short queries (15–40t), 25% medium (100–300t), 5% long summaries (up to 6k). Add burst windows to simulate up to 6x concurrency for 30s.
- Success criteria: p95 <= 220ms for short queries on the chosen model (rw-open-13b-quant) and qualitative parity on taxonomy labeling for 95% of sampled prompts.
- Regression guardrails: run prompt-set based automated eval (orbitai_promptset_v1.jsonl) each day of pilot; if quality drops >5% on key taxonomy buckets, trigger a rollback and notify CS + product. See attached checklist.
- Owner assignments: Monica — test harness and monitoring dashboards; Vivek — pricing & fallback policy sign-off; Ben — bench jobs and delivery of perf CSV + summary.

Attachment: qa-regression-checklist.md (Markdown, 4KB)

I’ll schedule a 30m internal prep at 2pm today if you can both make it.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
